lesson.title: Around and inside circles

lead.text: The radius runs from the centre of a circle to its edge. The diameter runs from edge to edge through the centre.
Radius and diameter measure different lengths. Check which one you are given.

steps.headline: A diameter is two radii laid end to end.

lead.text: The distance round a circle is its circumference. Divide it by the diameter and you always get the same number, π, about 3.14.
So circumference = π × diameter. In radius terms, that is 2 × π × radius.

steps.headline: The distance round a circle is about 3.14 times the distance across.
A circle has radius 5 cm. Find its circumference. Use π ≈ 3.14.

workedSteps.text: Double the radius to get the diameter.

steps.headline: A circle has radius 3 cm. Find its circumference. Use π ≈ 3.14.

lead.text: Area is the space inside, so it has square units. It uses the radius twice: π × r × r.
Square the radius, then multiply by π. Never use the diameter in place of the radius.

steps.headline: The space inside a circle is π × radius × radius.

lead.text: The mat's size is given across. Decide whether that is the radius or the diameter before you start.

reveal.text: Halve the diameter, square the radius, multiply by π. Using 8 as the radius would have made the area four times too big.

lead.text: Compare 2 × π × r with π × r × r. Ask how many times the radius appears in each.

lesson.orientation: Use radius and diameter correctly in circumference and circle-area calculations.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: A pizza has a 15 cm line from its middle to its edge.

intro.promise: By the end you'll find the distance round a circle and the space inside it, from either its radius or its diameter.

recap.keyIdea: The circumference is π × diameter and the area is π × radius × radius. Check which of radius and diameter you are given.

blocks.text: You found that a 15 cm middle-to-edge line makes a pizza 30 cm across.
You found 18.84 cm round a circle of radius 3 cm, and 50.24 m² for a mat 8 m across.

recap.nextHook: A bigger copy of a shape changes lengths and areas differently. Find out how much.

questions.prompt: A circle has radius 3 cm. Find its diameter in centimetres.
hints: The diameter crosses the entire circle through its centre.
It contains a radius on each side of the centre.
Multiply the radius by two.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: A diameter contains two radii: 2 × 3 = 6 cm.

questions.onCorrect: 6 cm. A diameter is two radii laid end to end.

misconceptions.feedback: 3 cm is the radius you were given. The diameter goes right across.
That halves the radius. The diameter is longer than the radius.

questions.prompt: A circle has radius 3 cm. Use π ≈ 3.14 to find its circumference in centimetres.
hints: Circumference measures the rim.
Multiply the diameter by π.
Calculate 2 × 3.14 × 3.
questions.onCorrect: 18.84 cm. Circumference is π × diameter, or 2 × π × radius.

misconceptions.feedback: 6 cm is only the diameter. Multiply it by π.
That is the area, which uses r × r. Circumference is the distance round.

questions.prompt: A disc has radius 3 cm. Use π ≈ 3.14 to find its area in square centimetres.
hints: Area covers the disc.
Square the radius, then multiply by π.
Calculate 3.14 × (3 × 3).
questions.onCorrect: 28.26 cm². Area is π × radius × radius.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the distance round. Area is the space inside: π × r × r.
That is π × 3. The radius is used twice: r × r.
That squares the radius but leaves out π.

questions.prompt: A circular mat is 8 m across. Use π ≈ 3.14 to find its area in square metres.
hints: The given distance is the diameter.
Halve it to obtain the radius before squaring.
Calculate 3.14 × (8/2)².
questions.onCorrect: 50.24 m². The mat is 8 across, so the radius is 4 before you square it.

misconceptions.feedback: That uses 8 as the radius. The mat is 8 across, which is the diameter.
That is π × 8. Area needs the radius multiplied by itself, then π.

questions.prompt: A circle's radius doubles. What happens to its circumference and its area?
hints: Compare 2πr with πr².

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Circumference contains one radius factor; area contains two, so their multipliers are 2 and 2².

questions.onCorrect: Circumference doubles and area quadruples. Circumference uses r once, area uses r twice.

misconceptions.feedback: Area uses the radius twice (r × r), so it grows by more than the radius does.
Circumference uses the radius once, so it grows only as fast as the radius.

questions.prompt: Which measurement determines the length of trim around a circular table?
hints: Identify whether you need the boundary or the covered surface.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Trim follows the one-dimensional boundary, so its length is the circumference.

questions.onCorrect: Its circumference. Trim runs along the edge, and the circumference is the distance round.

misconceptions.feedback: Area is the space inside. Trim runs along the edge.
Volume needs three dimensions. A table's edge is a length.

questions.prompt: How wide is the pizza across, measured straight through the middle, in centimetres?
hints: Picture the line from the middle to the edge. Now carry on to the opposite edge.
The line across the middle is made of two of the 15 cm lines.
Double the distance from the middle to the edge.
questions.onCorrect: 30 cm. Across the middle covers the distance from centre to edge twice.

misconceptions.feedback: 15 cm only goes from the middle to the edge. Across the middle goes further.
That halves it. Across the middle is longer than the middle-to-edge line.

questions.prompt: Why do we double the radius first?
hints: What does π multiply to give the circumference?

acceptedIdeas: The diameter is two radii, and circumference is π times the diameter.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The diameter is two radii, and circumference is π times the diameter.

choices.label: The diameter is two radii, and circumference is π times the diameter.
Because the radius is always too small.
Doubling is needed for every circle measurement.

questions.onCorrect: Circumference is π × diameter, and the diameter is two radii: 2 × π × r.

misconceptions.feedback: The radius isn't wrong. It just has to be doubled to get the diameter that π multiplies.
Area uses the radius itself, twice over. Doubling is for circumference.

questions.prompt: A circle has diameter 10 cm. Use π ≈ 3.14 to find its area in square centimetres.
hints: Halve the diameter to get the radius.
Multiply the radius by itself.
Multiply by 3.14.
questions.onCorrect: 78.5 cm². Halve the diameter to get 5, then π × 5 × 5.

misconceptions.feedback: That uses 10 as the radius. Halve the diameter first.
That is the distance round. Area is the space inside.

questions.prompt: A circular track has diameter 20 m. Use π ≈ 3.14 to find how far it is once round, in metres.
hints: The distance round is the circumference.
Circumference is π times the diameter.
Multiply 3.14 by 20.
questions.onCorrect: 62.8 m. Circumference is π × the diameter, here 3.14 × 20.

misconceptions.feedback: That is an area with radius 10. The distance round is π × diameter.
That doubles the diameter. Circumference is π × the diameter itself.

questions.prompt: A circle is 2 cm across. Use π ≈ 3.14 to find the distance round it, in centimetres.
hints: The distance round is π times the distance across.
The distance across is 2 cm.
Multiply 3.14 by 2.
questions.onCorrect: 6.28 cm. The distance round is π times the distance across.

misconceptions.feedback: 2 cm is the distance across. The distance round is π times that.
That doubles the 2 cm again. The 2 cm is already the whole way across.

citations.claim: Circumference = π × diameter = 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm.

Circumference is π times the diameter, with π about 3.14.
Circumference is π times the diameter, which is twice the radius.
